result:
I could not verify this from first principles, so the answer below is a tentative one.

The obvious sparse obstruction, $K_{2,n-2}$, has only $2(n-2)$ edges and no HIST. Adding edges inside its large side creates a HIST, so the extremal graph must be a different, much denser construction. I tried the natural candidate of a clique on $n-3$ vertices plus outside vertices of degree 2 attached to a common pair $\{a,b\}$. That construction does contain a HIST, so it is not an obstruction. I did not find a construction achieving $\binom{n-3}{2}+4$, and I did not find a proof that no denser non-HIST graph exists.

The other agent's value, $\binom{n-3}{2}+4$, is plausible in form, since such bounds for 2-connected graphs typically have this shape. I have not checked it against the literature, so I am carrying it forward without independent confirmation.

ANSWER: $\binom{n-3}{2}+4$
